title: Listening to the Sounds Around You
summary: Listen outward, then inward: surroundings and interior.
script:
Hello, and welcome to this “listening to the sounds around you meditation”. Take a moment to get comfortable and relax.
You can sit on the couch, sit on a pillow, or lie down on your bed. Find a position that feels comfortable for you today.
There’s no need to sit in a special position. Just let your body relax and take your time.
When you’re ready, you can gently close your eyes, or simply look down and let your eyes relax.
For the next few minutes, you don’t need to go anywhere or do anything. Just stay here, take a slow breath, and focus on this moment.
Feel the surface beneath you, holding you completely. Let your shoulders soften. Let your hands rest.
Take a slow breath in… and let it out.
Once more. In… and out.
Today, we're going to explore two words that describe two different worlds, the world outside of us, and the world within us.
The first is surroundings. Surroundings are the people, places, and things around you.
For example, when you sit in a quiet room, the room and everything around you are your surroundings.
The second is interior. "Interior" can mean the inside of you, your thoughts, feelings, or emotions.
For example, meditation can help you pay attention to your interior world, or what is happening inside you.
Today, we'll move gently between these two worlds, simply by listening.
Let's begin with your surroundings. Bring your attention to any sounds you can hear right now, outside of your body.
Maybe something close to you. Maybe something far away. Maybe silence itself, which has its own quiet sound.
Just listen. Notice these sounds as they come, and notice them as they disappear. There’s nothing to identify. Nothing to name. Just simple, open listening.
Notice how these sounds belong to your surroundings, existing outside of you, independent of your thoughts, independent of your breath.
Stay here for a moment, simply listening to your surroundings.
Now, gently, let's shift your attention inward, to your interior.
Notice your breath. This sound, this movement, belongs only to you. It exists inside your body, quiet and constant.
Listen to your breath the way you listened to those sounds around you. Notice it as it comes, and notice it as it goes, again and again.
This is your interior world. Quiet, and completely your own.
Take a slow breath in… and out.
Now, let's move gently back to your surroundings. Notice any sounds outside of you once again. The distant hum of something far away. The quiet stillness of the room. Whatever exists around you, right now.
Notice how these sounds continue, whether you're listening or not. Your surroundings simply exist, patient and constant.
Move your attention back inward now, to your interior. Notice your heartbeat, if you can feel it. Notice the quiet rhythm of your breath. Notice the stillness of your own thoughts, settling gently.
This interior world is always with you, wherever you go, wherever your surroundings might change.
Let's practice moving between these two worlds a little more. Bring your awareness outward, to your surroundings. Listen carefully.
And now, bring your awareness inward, to your interior. Listen just as carefully.
Notice how both worlds exist, at the very same time. Your surroundings, full of sound, full of space. Your interior, quiet, personal, and steady.
There's something valuable in noticing this difference. Often, our attention gets pulled entirely outward, toward our surroundings. We forget our interior world completely. Other times, we become so lost in our interior thoughts, we forget the world around us.
Today, you've simply practiced noticing both, gently moving between them, without needing to choose one over the other.
Let your awareness rest now, somewhere between these two worlds. Aware of your surroundings. Aware of your interior. Both present. Both welcome.
Let these gentle words settle into your mind.
I am aware of my surroundings.
I am aware of my interior.
Both worlds exist, together, in this moment.
I am calm.
I am present.
Take another slow breath, and let these words settle a little deeper.
Stay here for a while longer, simply noticing both worlds, your surroundings, and your interior, existing quietly, side by side.
There's no need to choose between them. Both are part of your experience, right now, and always.
When you feel ready, begin to bring a little more attention back to your surroundings. Notice the sounds around you. Notice the air, the space, the room you're sitting in.
Let your fingers move first, just slightly. Then your toes. Small movements, gentle and unhurried.
Take your time. There's no need to rush this return.
Whenever you're ready, let your eyes open softly, taking in your surroundings once again.
Carry this awareness with you, into the rest of your day. Notice, from time to time, both worlds, the sounds around you, and the quiet world within.
You are calm. You are present. And you are exactly where you need to be.

vocabulary.definition: the people, places, and things around you
everything inside you: your thoughts, feelings, and breath

exercises.sentence: My thoughts and feelings are part of my _____ world.
The room, the people, and the sounds around me are my _____.
